title: A vintage card has two prices
headline: A vintage card has two prices. The board has to pick one.
dek: TCGplayer prices some vintage cards twice: a 1st Edition printing and an Unlimited one, each with its own price. Of the 660 rows the board's lists have published since Oct 13, 21 name an edition (13 "1st Edition", 6 "1st Edition Holofoil", 2 "Unlimited Holofoil"), and not one card changed printing from one list to the next. That consistency is the point: a card is only ever compared with its own printing, so a move on the board is never one printing's price set against the other's. On Nov 14 we made the choice explicit for the price lookups behind the board as well: Unlimited first for the Wizards of the Coast printings, and 1st Edition only when we ask for it by name.
why_now: A vintage price with no printing attached is a price for a card nobody can name. Call #003 says "unlimited, raw" in its starting price for that reason. This week's build closed the last place that could pick a printing by accident, so it is the Saturday to say what the board does and what it can't yet show.
risk: What is confirmed is the board's own lists: 21 rows, none switching. What isn't: the pricing change merged on Nov 14 and goes live when Railway deploys it, so until a publish after that shows a vintage row reading "Unlimited Holofoil" it is untested in production. A row can change printing once on the day it deploys and is still compared only with its own printing, so it can't show a false move. Twenty-one rows is also a small slice, mostly Neo-era cards plus one Base Set (Shadowless) Dragonair. No sale was checked behind any of it. This is not a read on whether these prices are high or low.
what_to_watch: The first publish after the deploy: whether any vintage row now reads "Unlimited Holofoil" where it read "1st Edition" or nothing before, and that no row's printing then changes from night to night. Whether a 1st Edition card makes the 7-day list again; the three here were last listed in October. And what we haven't built: showing both printings' prices side by side for one card.
source: TCGplayer market prices via tcgcsv.com, from the board's published lists, Oct 13 to Nov 14, 2026 (33 mornings, 660 rows); Mission Control's pricing settings as merged Nov 14, 2026

foot: Market price: TCGplayer's average of recent completed sales of the same card, condition and printing (help.tcgplayer.com). The counts: the board's own published lists, Oct 13 to Nov 14, 2026, 33 mornings (git history of data/movers.json): 330 rows in the 7-day list and 330 in the since-yesterday list, 660 in all. Each row carries a variant field naming the printing: 608 "Holofoil", 31 blank, 13 "1st Edition", 6 "1st Edition Holofoil", 2 "Unlimited Holofoil". No card id appears with more than one variant. The table: three cards that name an edition, each at its last 7-day list appearance (Heracross, Neo Genesis; Light Jolteon, Neo Destiny; Dragonair, Base Set Shadowless); start-of-week prices are worked back from the listed price and its rounded change, so within a dollar. The list: up to 10 Pokémon cards worth $20 or more that moved 5% or more in a week; with no checked sales, a move shows only if it's 60% or less, the lowest listing moved the same way by at least a quarter as much, the price changed in the last 2 days, and the card trades. Unconfirmed: no sale checked by Mission Control's Sale Integrity Layer in that window. Not advice.
